question: What is the regulatory definition of a specialty occupation for H-1B purposes?
expected_answer: An occupation requiring theoretical and practical application of a highly specialized body of knowledge plus a bachelor's or higher degree (or equivalent) in the specific specialty as a minimum for entry
agent_answer:
## Regulatory Definition of a Specialty Occupation for H-1B Purposes

Based on the available corpus, a **specialty occupation** for H-1B purposes is defined as follows:

> *"A specialty occupation is one that requires the theoretical and practical application of a body of highly specialized knowledge to fully perform the occupation and requires the attainment of a bachelor's or higher degree in a directly related specific specialty, or its equivalent, as a minimum for entry into the occupation in the United States."*

[Source: USCIS Form I-129 Instructions](https://www.uscis.gov/sites/default/files/document/forms/i-129instr.pdf)

### Key Clarifications Provided in the Same Source:

- **A general degree is insufficient**: *"A position is not a specialty occupation if attainment of a general degree, without further specialization, is sufficient to qualify for the position."*
- **Range of qualifying degree fields is permissible**, provided *each* field is **directly related** to the duties of the position.
- **"Directly related"** means *"there is a logical connection between the degree, or its equivalent, and the duties of the position."*

The USCIS H-1B Cap Season page also lists example fields, including architecture, engineering, mathematics, sciences, medicine, law, and the arts. [Source: USCIS H-1B Cap Season](https://www.uscis.gov/working-in-the-united-states/temporary-workers/h-1b-specialty-occupations/h-1b-cap-season)

question: Must an F-1 student maintain a full course of study to keep status?
expected_answer: Yes -- F-1 undergraduate students must take at least 12 credit hours per term; graduate students must take a full course of study as certified by the institution
agent_answer:
## F-1 Student Full Course of Study Requirement

Yes, maintaining a full course of study is a fundamental requirement for F-1 student status.

### General Requirement
According to the Department of Homeland Security, to maintain F-1 status, a student **must enroll in a full course of study** at the SEVP-certified school where their Form I-20 was issued. [studyinthestates.dhs.gov](https://studyinthestates.dhs.gov/students/full-course-of-study)

### Specific Credit Hour Requirements
For post-secondary F-1 students, the requirements are:
- **Undergraduate students** at a college or university: at least **12 credit hours per term**
- **Postgraduate students**: a full course of study as certified by the institution
- **Other post-secondary programs**: 18 clock hours/week (classroom majority) or 22 clock hours/week (non-classroom majority) [studyinthestates.dhs.gov](https://studyinthestates.dhs.gov/students/full-course-of-study)

### Limited Exceptions (Reduced Course Load)
A DSO may authorize a reduced course load **only** for:
1. Specified initial academic difficulties (once per program level)
2. Temporary illness or medical condition (aggregate maximum of 12 months)
3. Final term completion needs

**A student who drops below a full course of study without prior DSO approval is considered out of status.** [uscis.gov](https://www.uscis.gov/policy-manual/volume-2-part-f-chapter-3)

### Important Note on Online Courses
Only **one class or three credits per term** taken online may count toward the full course of study requirement for F-1 students. [studyinthestates.dhs.gov](https://studyinthestates.dhs.gov/students/full-course-of-study)

---

question: What prior employment abroad is generally required before an L-1 intracompany transfer?

## L-1 Prior Foreign Employment Requirements

Based on the USCIS Policy Manual, the following foreign employment requirements must generally be met before an L-1 intracompany transfer:

### Duration of Employment
The beneficiary must have been **employed abroad continuously for 1 year out of the 3 years preceding the application** for admission to the United States. [uscis.gov/policy-manual/volume-2-part-l-chapter-2](https://www.uscis.gov/policy-manual/volume-2-part-l-chapter-2)

### Nature of the Employment
That 1 year of continuous employment abroad must have been in one of the following capacities:
- **Managerial capacity**
- **Executive capacity**
- **Specialized knowledge capacity**

[uscis.gov/policy-manual/volume-2-part-l-chapter-2](https://www.uscis.gov/policy-manual/volume-2-part-l-chapter-2)

### Key Additional Details
- The 1-year requirement must be satisfied **physically outside the United States** — time spent working in the U.S. does not count toward this requirement, even if paid by the foreign entity. [uscis.gov/policy-manual/volume-2-part-l-chapter-6](https://www.uscis.gov/policy-manual/volume-2-part-l-chapter-6)
- The requirement must be met **at the time the L-1 petition is filed**. [uscis.gov/policy-manual/volume-2-part-l-chapter-6](https://www.uscis.gov/policy-manual/volume-2-part-l-chapter-6)
- Brief B-1/B-2 visits to the U.S. **toll** (pause) — but do not break — the continuity of the 1-year period. [uscis.gov/policy-manual/volume-2-part-l-chapter-6](https://www.uscis.gov/policy-manual/volume-2-part-l-chapter-6)
- The beneficiary **does not need to be transferred in the same capacity** in which they worked abroad (e.g., a foreign manager could transfer to a specialized knowledge role in the U.S.). [uscis.gov/policy-manual/volume-2-part-l-chapter-2](https://www.uscis.gov/policy-manual/volume-2-part-l-chapter-2)

question: What is the general standard for O-1 extraordinary ability classification?

## O-1 Extraordinary Ability Classification Standards

Based on the USCIS Policy Manual, the O-1 classification encompasses different standards depending on the specific field:

### O-1A (Sciences, Education, Business, or Athletics)
The beneficiary must demonstrate **"sustained national or international acclaim"** and represent **"a level of expertise indicating that the person is one of the small percentage who have arisen to the very top of the field of endeavor."**
[Source](https://www.uscis.gov/policy-manual/volume-2-part-m-chapter-4)

### O-1B (Arts)
The beneficiary must show **"distinction"** — defined as **"a high level of achievement in the field of arts, as evidenced by a degree of skill and recognition substantially above that ordinarily encountered"** to the extent that the person is **renowned, leading, or well-known** in the field.
[Source](https://www.uscis.gov/policy-manual/volume-2-part-m-chapter-4)

### O-1B (Motion Picture & Television)
The beneficiary must have a **"demonstrated record of extraordinary achievement"** reflecting **"a very high level of accomplishment"** such that the person is **recognized as outstanding, notable, or leading** in the field.
[Source](https://www.uscis.gov/policy-manual/volume-2-part-m-chapter-4)

### Universal Requirement
In **all cases**, achievements must be **"recognized in the field through extensive documentation."**
[Source](https://www.uscis.gov/policy-manual/volume-2-part-m-chapter-4)

The STEM OPT extension is a program that allows eligible F-1 students to extend their post-completion Optional Practical Training (OPT) period by an additional **24 months**, resulting in a **maximum total of 36 months** of OPT authorization.

- **Who qualifies:** F-1 students who hold a bachelor's, master's, or doctoral degree in a field with a CIP (Classification of Instructional Programs) code that appears on the **DHS STEM Designated Degree Program List**. [uscis.gov](https://www.uscis.gov/policy-manual/volume-2-part-f-chapter-5)

- **Lifetime maximum:** A student may receive up to **two STEM OPT extensions** if they earn qualifying STEM degrees at different educational levels. [uscis.gov](https://www.uscis.gov/policy-manual/volume-2-part-f-chapter-5)

question: If an F-1 student on OPT is in H-1B "cap-gap" status waiting for an October 1 start, what happens to their work authorization in the interim?
expected_answer: As of a January 17, 2025 DHS final rule, eligible F-1 students with a timely-filed cap-subject H-1B petition get an automatic extension of both F-1 status and work authorization until April 1 of the relevant fiscal year (extended from the previous October 1 cutoff). This bridges the gap between the end of F-1/OPT status and the H-1B start date.
agent_answer:
## F-1 Cap-Gap Work Authorization During the Interim Period

### Automatic Extension of OPT Employment Authorization

If an F-1 student is **currently authorized for OPT employment** when their employer files a timely H-1B cap-subject petition, their work authorization is **automatically extended** through the cap-gap period — they do not need to take separate action to obtain this extension.

Specifically, the cap-gap extension automatically extends both F-1 status **and** post-completion OPT (including STEM OPT) employment authorization until October 1, when H-1B status begins. [USCIS Policy Manual](https://www.uscis.gov/policy-manual/volume-2-part-f-chapter-5)

---

### Key Conditions That Must Be Met

For OPT employment authorization to be extended, the student must:
- Be **currently authorized for OPT** at the time the H-1B petition is filed
- Not have violated the terms of their nonimmigrant status
- Have an H-1B petition that was **timely filed** requesting an October 1 start date
[USCIS Policy Manual](https://www.uscis.gov/policy-manual/volume-2-part-f-chapter-5)

---

### Important Limitations

| Situation | Work Authorization Outcome |
|-----------|---------------------------|
| Student was on OPT when H-1B was filed | ✅ OPT extended through cap-gap |
| Student was in **60-day grace period** (not on OPT) when H-1B was filed | ❌ F-1 status extended, but **no work authorization** |
| H-1B petition denied, withdrawn, or revoked | ❌ Work authorization ends; 60-day grace period to depart |

[USCIS Policy Manual](https://www.uscis.gov/policy-manual/volume-2-part-f-chapter-5)

---

### No New EAD Card Issued

Importantly, **USCIS will not issue a new or renewed Employment Authorization Document (EAD)** during the cap-gap period. The student's proof of continued status and work authorization is an **updated Form I-20** annotated by their Designated School Official (DSO) for the cap-gap extension. [State Department FAM](https://fam.state.gov/FAM/09FAM/09FAM040205.html); [Study in the States](https://studyinthestates.dhs.gov/students/h-1b-status-and-the-cap-gap-extension)

---

### Unemployment During Cap-Gap

Any unemployment during the cap-gap automatic extension **counts toward the cumulative maximum** allowed unemployment days (90 days for post-completion OPT, or 150 days for STEM OPT). [USCIS Policy Manual](https://www.uscis.gov/policy-manual/volume-2-part-f-chapter-5)

---

>

question: How do the SEVIS record requirements for F-1 dependents (F-2) relate to the principal student's program end date?

## SEVIS Record Requirements for F-2 Dependents Relative to the F-1 Program End Date

### Current Rules (Pre-September 15, 2026)

Under the current **duration of status** framework, F-2 dependents' SEVIS records are directly tied to the F-1 principal student's status and program end date in several key ways:

---

### 1. Extensions of Stay
- F-2 dependents **do not need to apply separately** for an extension of stay if the F-1 student cannot complete their course of study by the program end date on Form I-20.
- When a DSO grants a program extension to the F-1 student, **the DSO updates SEVIS for both the F-1 student and the F-2 dependents simultaneously.** [(USCIS Policy Manual, Vol. 2, Part F, Ch. 8)](https://www.uscis.gov/policy-manual/volume-2-part-f-chapter-8)

---

### 2. Record Terminations
- If a student's SEVIS record is terminated, **any associated F-2 dependent records are also terminated automatically**, meaning dependents immediately lose their authorized period of stay. [(Study in the States – Maintaining Accurate SEVIS Records)](https://studyinthestates.dhs.gov/schools/report/maintaining-accurate-sevis-records)

---

### 3. Transfers After Program Completion
- DSOs must initiate transfer of the F-1 student's SEVIS record to a new school **within 60 days of the program end date**, which also affects dependent status continuity. [(Study in the States – K-12 Schools)](https://studyinthestates.dhs.gov/schools/get-started/kindergarten-to-grade-12-schools)

---

### 4. Post-September 15, 2026 Change
- After the final rule takes effect, F-2 dependents will also require an extension of stay beyond their **Admit Until Date**, and any extension **may not exceed the authorized period of admission for the principal F-1 student.** [(Study in the States – Final Rule FAQ)](https://studyinthestates.dhs.gov/final-rule-establishing-a-fixed-time-period-of-admission-and-an-extension-of-stay-procedure-faq)

---

### Key Takeaway
The F-2 dependent's SEVIS record is essentially **derivative of and dependent upon** the F-1 principal's record — extensions, terminations, and transfers all flow directly from changes made to the principal student's record.

---

question: What is the difference between CPT and OPT for F-1 students?
expected_answer: CPT is training that is an integral part of an established curriculum, authorized while the student maintains a full course of study; OPT is practical training related to the student's major used before or after completing the program of study, and unlike CPT it is authorized by USCIS (via Form I-765) rather than just the DSO
agent_answer:
## CPT vs. OPT for F-1 Students

Here is a comparison of the key differences between Curricular Practical Training (CPT) and Optional Practical Training (OPT) for F-1 students:

---

### **Timing**
- **CPT** can only occur **before** the student's program end date — it is exclusively available during the course of study. ([USCIS Policy Manual](https://www.uscis.gov/policy-manual/volume-2-part-f-chapter-5))
- **OPT** can be authorized **both during** (pre-completion) and **after** (post-completion) the student's degree program. ([FAM 9 FAM 402.5-5(N)(5)](https://fam.state.gov/FAM/09FAM/09FAM040205.html))

---

### **Relationship to Curriculum**
- **CPT** must be an **integral part of an established curriculum** — typically required internships or practicums offered through cooperative agreements with the school. ([USCIS Policy Manual](https://www.uscis.gov/policy-manual/volume-2-part-f-chapter-5))
- **OPT** must be **directly related to the major area of study**, but does not need to be a required curriculum component. ([Study in the States](https://studyinthestates.dhs.gov/students/work/applying-for-practical-training))

---

### **Authorization Process**
- **CPT** is authorized **solely by the DSO**, who endorses the Form I-20. **No application to USCIS and no Employment Authorization Document (EAD) is required.** ([USCIS Policy Manual](https://www.uscis.gov/policy-manual/volume-2-part-f-chapter-5))
- **OPT** requires the student to **file Form I-765 with USCIS** and receive an **EAD** before beginning work. ([Study in the States](https://studyinthestates.dhs.gov/students/work/applying-for-practical-training))

---

### **Hours/Schedule**
- **CPT** may be part-time or full-time and is **not restricted by a 20-hour weekly limit.** ([Study in the States](https://studyinthestates.dhs.gov/students/work/applying-for-practical-training))
- **OPT (pre-completion)** is limited to **20 hours per week while school is in session**; post-completion OPT must be **at least 20 hours per week.** ([Study in the States](https://studyinthestates.dhs.gov/students/work/applying-for-practical-training))
